answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may place orders, then slash that stake when peers prove a signed order was fraudulent. Splitting one operator into a plume of aliases does not multiply its capital: every alias must fund its own bond, and each exposed identity risks losing it. A sparrow-sized account can still participate, but flooding a ridge of markets with fake agents ties up funds and makes each detected lie costly.
